In response to higher operating activity, accounts payable also increased during the first quarter of 2026 compared to year end 2025. Inventory levels decreased, reflecting efforts to proactively manage inventory while supporting customer demand in the subsequent quarter.

capex.text: During the three months ended March 31, 2026, Titan reported a net cash outflow from investing activities of $13.1 million, as compared to the $14.8 million outflow recorded in the corresponding period of 2025. This change was primarily due to lower capital expenditures in 2026. The reduction in capital spending in 2026 reflected Titan's efforts to optimize cashflow management. These capital expenditures were aimed at replacing and enhancing plant equipment, as well as acquiring new tools, dies, and molds to support new product development initiatives.

net sales.heading: Net Sales
net sales.text: Net sales for the three months ended March 31, 2026 were $505.1 million, compared to $490.7 million in the comparable period of 2025. The increase was driven by foreign currency translation, which contributed approximately 3.7% to net sales growth, largely due to the strengthening of the Brazilian real and euro against the U.S. dollar and favorable pricing related to higher input costs. These increases were partially offset by lower sales volumes resulting from reduced customer demand in the consumer and agricultural segments due to challenging market conditions.

tax.heading: Provision for Income Taxes
tax.text:
The Company recorded income tax (benefit) expense of $0.0 million and $4.7 million for the three months ended June 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively. For the six months ended June 30, 2026 and 2025, the Company recorded income tax expense of $4.6 million and $8.9 million, respectively. The Company's effective income tax rate was (0.1)% and 431.6% for the three months ended June 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively, and (34.9)% and 167.1% for the six months ended June 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively. For the six months ended June 30, 2026 and 2025, the income tax expense differed each period due to an overall decrease in foreign pre-tax income slightly offset by a valuation allowance on the domestic operations, and certain discrete tax benefits recorded in 2026.

The Company’s 2026 and 2025 income tax expense and rates differed from the amount of income tax determined by applying the U.S. Federal income tax rate to pre-tax income primarily as a result of foreign income tax rate differential on the mix of earnings and a valuation allowance on most domestic federal and state operations.

Net sales was primarily driven by higher sales volumes in the Titan Specialty business, reflecting improved demand compared to the prior year period. The increase was also contributed by favorable pricing, which reflected higher input costs, and an improved product mix. In addition, the increase benefited from favorable foreign currency translation, which contributed approximately 2.4% to net sales growth, largely due to the strengthening of the Brazilian real against the U.S. dollar.

Net sales for the six months ended June 30, 2026 were $989.8 million, compared to $951.5 million in the comparable period of 2025. The increase was supported by favorable pricing due to higher input costs, and an improved product mix, and was primarily driven by favorable foreign currency translation, which contributed approximately 3.1% to net sales growth, largely due to the strengthening of the Brazilian real and euro against the U.S. dollar.

The change was primarily due to lower capital expenditures in 2026. Capital expenditures were primarily related to plant equipment upgrades, productivity initiatives, and tools, dies and molds supporting new product development. The reduction in capital spending in 2026 reflected Titan's continued focus on optimizing cash flow and capital deployment.

net sales.heading: Net Sales
net sales.text:
Net sales for the three months ended September 30, 2026 were $335.2 million, compared to $357.3 million in the comparable period of 2025, primarily due to lower sales volumes resulting from reduced end‑market demand due to weak market conditions, partially offset by favorable pricing, which reflected higher input costs and improved product mix. In addition, favorable foreign currency translation contributed approximately 0.2% to net sales growth.

Net sales for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 were $1,096.6 million, compared to $1,086.8 million in the comparable period of 2025. The increase was primarily driven by favorable pricing reflecting higher input costs, improved product mix, and favorable foreign currency translation, which increased net sales by approximately 1.5%, primarily due to the strengthening of the Brazilian real against the U.S. dollar. These increases were partially offset by lower sales volumes in the agricultural segment, reflecting softer end-market demand.

Headquartered in West Chicago, Illinois, the Company globally produces a broad range of products to meet the specifications of original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) and aftermarket customers in the agricultural, earthmoving/construction, and consumer markets. For more information, visit www.titan-intl.com.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Equity-method investments
lines.why: Stakes in associated businesses, usually part of operations. Financial if held as an investment.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Wages, services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Pension and retiree benefits
lines.why: Promised to employees for their work: operating (some analysts treat the unfunded part as debt).

lines.name: Deferred revenue, non-current
lines.why: Customers' payments for later years: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.
